questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: The library advertises that all of its services are free and open to everyone. [[However,]] it lends out laptops only to students who can prove financial need.
questions.explanation: A laptop policy limited to students in financial need contradicts the claim that every service is open to everyone, so the contrast word 'However' fits; 'In addition' would extend the claim rather than reverse it, 'As a result' signals cause and effect, and 'For example' would wrongly offer the restriction as proof of openness.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: Heavy rain fell across the valley all night. [[For example,]] the river overflowed its banks by morning.
questions.explanation: The overflowing river is the effect of the heavy rain, so the cause/effect word 'As a result' fits; 'For example' introduces an illustration, 'Nevertheless' contrast, and 'Likewise' comparison, none of which match.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: First, spread the glue evenly across the cardboard. [[However,]] press the two pieces firmly together.
questions.explanation: The sentences describe steps in order, so the sequence word 'Then' fits; 'However' signals contrast, 'In fact' emphasis, and 'For example' an illustration, none of which suits a step-by-step process.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: The forecast promised clear skies for the parade. [[Therefore,]] a sudden downpour soaked the marchers.
questions.explanation: The downpour clashes with the promise of clear skies, so the contrast word 'However' fits; 'Therefore' implies a result, while 'Similarly' and 'In addition' signal agreement, none of which match the reversal.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: Earthworms enrich the soil with nutrients from their waste. [[On the other hand,]] their burrowing can speed erosion on steep, bare slopes.
questions.explanation: A drawback set against a benefit calls for a contrast, so 'On the other hand' fits; 'Furthermore' signals addition, 'As a result' cause and effect, and 'For instance' an example, none of which match the trade-off.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: Everyone expected the rookie to be nervous in his first game. [[Consequently,]] he played with the calm of a veteran.
questions.explanation: His calm play reverses the expectation of nervousness, so the contrast word 'Instead' fits; 'Consequently' signals a result, 'For example' an illustration, and 'Likewise' agreement, none of which capture the reversal.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: The hard drive had not been backed up in months. [[In other words,]] the crash wiped out years of irreplaceable photos.
questions.explanation: The missing backups led to the loss of the photos, so the cause/effect word 'Thus' fits; 'In other words' restates an idea, 'Nevertheless' contrasts, and 'For instance' gives an example, none of which match the cause and result.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: The brochure described the resort as peaceful and quiet. [[Meanwhile,]] construction crews pounded away outside our window all week.
questions.explanation: The noisy construction contradicts the promise of peace and quiet, so the contrast word 'Yet' fits; 'Meanwhile' signals simultaneous time, 'So' a result, and 'Furthermore' addition, none of which signal the contradiction.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: Skeptics warned that the new bike lanes would sit empty and waste money. [[Nevertheless,]] the number of daily cyclists has doubled.
questions.explanation: The doubling of cyclists defies the skeptics' prediction of empty lanes, so the contrast word 'Nevertheless' fits; 'As a result' signals cause and effect, 'Likewise' comparison, and 'For example' an illustration, none of which match the surprise.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: First the chef chopped the onions and set them in a bowl. [[Therefore,]] she rinsed the cutting board and reached for the carrots.
questions.explanation: The two actions are simply ordered steps, so the time word 'Afterward' fits. 'Therefore' forces a cause-effect link that rinsing the board does not have with chopping, 'In contrast' signals a clash, and 'For example' signals an illustration, none of which match a plain sequence.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: People often picture sharks as relentless hunters. [[In fact,]] most species are slow-moving and rarely attack humans.
questions.explanation: The second sentence corrects a common misconception, which 'In fact' emphasizes; 'Therefore' implies a result, 'Likewise' agreement, and 'Meanwhile' simultaneous time, none of which fit a correction.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: The intern sorted the survey responses by region. [[Still,]] she entered each batch into the database.
questions.explanation: Entering the responses is the step that follows sorting them, so the sequence word 'Next' fits; 'Still' signals contrast, 'Likewise' comparison, and 'In other words' restatement, none of which suit the second step in a process.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: The diner had great food and a prime location on Main Street. [[Similarly,]] it shut its doors after barely a year in business.
questions.explanation: Closing despite clear advantages is a surprise, so the contrast word 'Nevertheless' fits; 'Similarly' and 'Indeed' signal agreement or emphasis, and 'Consequently' a result, none of which match the unexpected failure.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: Wetlands filter pollutants out of the water that flows through them. [[For instance,]] they store floodwater that would otherwise swamp nearby towns.
questions.explanation: Storing floodwater is a second benefit added to filtering pollutants, so the addition word 'Moreover' fits; 'For instance' would wrongly make flood storage an example of filtering, while 'However' and 'As a result' misstate the relationship.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: An older bridge nearby had buckled in a single strong storm. [[In contrast,]] the new span held firm in the season's worst gales.
questions.explanation: The new span's strength is set against the old bridge's collapse, so the contrast phrase 'In contrast' fits; 'As a result' signals cause and effect, 'Likewise' comparison, and 'For instance' an example, none of which match the opposition between the two bridges.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: Conservationists released a dozen beavers into the empty stream bed. [[For instance,]] the dams they built transformed it into a lush marsh.
questions.explanation: The marsh forms later, after the release, so the time word 'Eventually' fits; 'For instance' would wrongly make the dams an example of the release, while 'On the other hand' signals contrast and 'Likewise' comparison, neither of which suits a change that develops over time.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: The museum stays open late on Fridays. [[Instead,]] it offers guided tours every weekend morning.
questions.explanation: The weekend tours are a second offering added to the late Friday hours, so the addition word 'Additionally' fits; 'Instead' signals replacement, 'For example' an illustration, and 'Therefore' a result, none of which match.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: During the blackout, every house on the block sat dark and silent. [[Likewise,]] the traffic lights at each intersection went black.
questions.explanation: The dark traffic lights mirror the dark houses, so the comparison word 'Likewise' fits; 'However' signals contrast, 'Therefore' cause and effect, and 'For instance' an example, none of which capture the parallel between the two scenes.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees. [[In contrast,]] line the baking sheet with parchment paper.
questions.explanation: Lining the sheet happens during the same window as the oven heating up, so the time word 'Meanwhile' fits; 'In contrast' signals a clash, 'Therefore' a result, and 'For instance' an example, none of which suit two simultaneous tasks.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: Many people assume cactuses need almost no care. [[Likewise,]] overwatering is the most common reason they die.
questions.explanation: The second sentence emphasizes a surprising truth that corrects the assumption, so the emphasis word 'In fact' fits; 'Likewise' signals agreement, 'Therefore' a result, and 'Meanwhile' simultaneous time, none of which match.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: Coach Rivera goes out of her way for her players. [[Therefore,]] she shows up early to set out every cone herself.
questions.explanation: Setting out every cone herself is one concrete illustration of how she goes out of her way, so 'For example' fits; 'Therefore' signals a result, 'Nevertheless' contrast, and 'Likewise' comparison, none of which introduce an example.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: The startup poured money into flashy advertising that drew few new users. [[Moreover,]] it ignored the bugs customers kept reporting.
questions.explanation: Ignoring the bugs is a second, separate misstep added to the wasted ad spending, so the addition word 'Moreover' fits; 'As a result' signals cause and effect, 'In other words' a restatement, and 'For instance' an example, none of which match a second failing.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: The trail map warned that the summit route was strenuous. [[Consequently,]] we reached the top without breaking a sweat.
questions.explanation: Reaching the top easily reverses the warning about a strenuous climb, so the contrast word 'However' fits; 'Consequently' signals a result, 'Likewise' agreement, and 'In addition' addition, none of which capture the reversal.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: The committee reviewed every grant application twice. [[For example,]] it ranked the finalists by overall impact.
questions.explanation: Ranking the finalists is the last step after reviewing the applications, so the sequence word 'Finally' fits; 'For example' signals an illustration, 'However' contrast, and 'In fact' emphasis, none of which suit an ordered process.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: Solar panels cut a household's monthly electric bill. [[Nevertheless,]] they raise the resale value of the home.
questions.explanation: Raising resale value is a second advantage added to the lower bills, so the addition phrase 'What is more' fits; 'Nevertheless' signals contrast, 'For instance' an example, and 'Otherwise' a condition, none of which match a second benefit.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: Critics dismissed the novel as too long and slow. [[As a result,]] it went on to win the year's top literary prize.
questions.explanation: Winning the prize clashes with the harsh dismissal, so the contrast phrase 'Even so' fits; 'As a result' signals a result, 'In other words' restatement, and 'Likewise' agreement, none of which match the surprising outcome.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: The volunteers cleared the brush from the riverbank. [[In contrast,]] they planted native grasses to hold the soil in place.
questions.explanation: Planting the grasses is the step that follows clearing the brush, so the sequence word 'Next' fits; 'In contrast' signals a clash, 'Therefore' a result, and 'For example' an illustration, none of which suit an ordered process.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: Honeybees do far more than make honey for our tables. [[Therefore,]] they pollinate roughly a third of the crops we eat.
questions.explanation: Pollinating crops is a concrete example of the bigger role bees play, so the example word 'For instance' fits; 'Therefore' signals a result, 'However' contrast, and 'Meanwhile' simultaneous time, none of which match an illustration.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: Some readers think a thesaurus makes their writing stronger. [[Therefore,]] swapping in fancy synonyms often makes a sentence harder to follow.
questions.explanation: The second sentence emphasizes the true result that undercuts the assumption, so the emphasis phrase 'In reality' fits; 'Therefore' signals a result, 'Similarly' agreement, and 'Afterward' time order, none of which match a correction.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: The avenue's makeover changed daily life on the street in visible ways. [[For example,]] foot traffic to the shops along it climbed sharply.
questions.explanation: The surge in foot traffic is one concrete instance of the visible changes, so the example phrase 'For example' fits; 'Nonetheless' signals contrast, 'Beforehand' earlier time, and 'Therefore' cause and effect, none of which suit an illustration.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: Deep-sea anglerfish dangle a glowing lure to draw in prey. [[As a result,]] some species use the same light to signal potential mates.
questions.explanation: Signaling mates is a second use of the light added to luring prey, so the addition word 'Furthermore' fits; 'As a result' signals a result, 'Even so' contrast, and 'For instance' an example, none of which match a second function.

questions.questionText: Which transition is the most logical in context?
questions.stem: The archivists spent a decade digitizing the fragile manuscripts. [[Otherwise,]] the originals could be sealed away from light and humidity.
questions.explanation: Sealing the originals is the long-awaited step that comes after a decade of work, so the time phrase 'At last' fits; 'Otherwise' signals a condition, 'Conversely' contrast, and 'For example' an illustration, none of which suit the delayed outcome.
